integrity: The proof rewrites the exact beta norm as a gamma ratio and applies Taylor's theorem with a trigamma remainder. Because the intermediate gamma argument is always at least one half, the remainder is bounded uniformly for every b>=0. The phase laws then follow from the standard digamma asymptotic; numerical evaluation is only a consistency check.
scientific_limitations: The theorem analyzes only the parameter range where the cited source has already proved the exact beta-function operator norm, namely fixed alpha>-1 with p>=2(alpha+2). It does not enlarge the unresolved exact-norm range, and it does not address simultaneous variation of alpha, spectra, essential norms, compactness, or extremizers.
title: Critical high-\(p\) damping for generalized Hilbert norms
